best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: p2 is the best overall trade-off because it achieved perfect quality on this task while also being the fastest executed plan. Although p1 was cheaper, it missed the true counts by 2 reviews, and p3/p4 were either less accurate or not meaningfully cheaper. For a small dataset of 120 matching reviews, the extra cost of p2 is justified by exact results.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model helped compare semantic-classification variants before execution and highlighted that the sem_map operator dominated both cost and latency. In execution, GPT-4.1-mini delivered the best quality and fastest end-to-end runtime for review-text sentiment classification, while GPT-4.1-nano was cheaper but slightly less accurate. Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite looked promising in estimates, but observed runs showed much higher token output and worse accuracy, so it was not the best choice.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "sentiment",
        "type": str,
        "description": "Classify the review text as exactly one of: positive, negative."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GPT_4_1_NANO,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby(["sentiment"], ["count"], ["reviewId"])
pipeline.project(["sentiment", "count(reviewId)"])
pipeline
